idiom_name: Subject value in context.Context under an unexported key + SubjectFrom accessor
implementation_notes: Go has no framework identity type, and the community idiom is smaller than the classic structure: define a small struct for the descriptor, have the authentication middleware resolve the credential once and store the value on the request context with context.WithValue using an unexported key type, and expose one typed accessor so handlers never type-assert raw context values. Keep the struct immutable (or store it by value) so downstream code cannot rewrite the identity mid-request. The full authenticator/factory/descriptor structure is only justified when several credential mechanisms must be registered dynamically; otherwise a middleware plus an accessor is the whole pattern.
pitfalls: Exported or string context keys collide across packages; context.WithValue documents that keys should be a package-private comparable type (the unexported struct above) and that values carry request-scoped data only.
A context value smuggled into a background goroutine outlives the request: the Subject is then logged or used long after the credential stopped being valid.
Storing a pointer lets any handler mutate the descriptor; keep it immutable or pass value copies, and never place the raw credential under the same context key.
